records.source: חֲזוֹן֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־אָמ֔וֹץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה עַל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם בִּימֵ֨י עֻזִּיָּ֧הוּ יוֹתָ֛ם אָחָ֥ז יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: [The] vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in [the] days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
pieces: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz: what he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.

L.1: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, [and] Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

R.1: Isaiah son of Amoz saw these things in visions from God. They were about Judah and its capital city, Jerusalem. He saw them while Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.

decisions.choice: vision: what God showed the prophet, his message as a whole
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb "he saw" come from the same root. A "vision" here is not one dream or sight but the whole message God revealed to Isaiah, and the verse is the title of the book (compare Obadiah 1; Nahum 1:1; 2 Chronicles 32:32, which speaks of "the vision of Isaiah").

decisions.choice: Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah: kings of Judah in the second half of the eighth century BC
decisions.reason: Isaiah's call came in the year King Uzziah died (6:1). He spoke to Ahaz during the Syrian and Israelite threat (chapter 7) and to Hezekiah during the Assyrian invasion of 701 BC (chapters 36-39). The book thus covers some forty years or more of his work (2 Kings 15-20).

decisions.choice: saw these things in visions from God ... its capital city
decisions.reason: Readable says where the vision came from and explains that Jerusalem was Judah's capital. Both are clear from the book itself.

records.heading: Children who rebelled

records.source: שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּ֑ר בָּנִים֙ גִּדַּ֣לְתִּי וְרוֹמַ֔מְתִּי וְהֵ֖ם פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי׃
records.gloss: Hear, heavens, and give ear, earth, for Yahweh has spoken: children I have raised and brought up, and they have rebelled against me.
pieces: Listen, heavens; earth, open your ears, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken: \q I raised children and made them great, \q but they have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.2: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken: \q Children I have reared and brought up, \q and they have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.2: Sky, listen! Earth, listen! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken. He says: \q I raised children and helped them grow up. \q But they have turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: hear, heavens ... give ear, earth: heaven and earth called as witnesses
decisions.reason: Moses called heaven and earth to witness the covenant and Israel's coming unfaithfulness (Deuteronomy 30:19; 31:28), and his song opens with the same two verbs (Deuteronomy 32:1). Isaiah begins as if in a court case: God brings a charge against his people, with all creation listening (compare Micah 6:1-2).

decisions.choice: rebelled: broken faith with their lord
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a subject people breaking away from their overlord (2 Kings 1:1; 8:20). Israel's sin is pictured as children rising against the father who raised them.

decisions.choice: God's words begin without a mark
decisions.reason: After "Yahweh has spoken" the voice changes to God's own "I" with no word such as "saying". The prophet's words and God's are woven together through the chapter.

decisions.choice: sky ... He says: ... helped them grow up
decisions.reason: Readable says "sky" for the heavens, adds "He says" to show that God is now speaking, and puts the two verbs of raising ("made great" and "lifted high") as "raised ... and helped them grow up".

records.source: יָדַ֥ע שׁוֹר֙ קֹנֵ֔הוּ וַחֲמ֖וֹר אֵב֣וּס בְּעָלָ֑יו יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע עַמִּ֖י לֹ֥א הִתְבּוֹנָֽן׃
records.gloss: Knows an ox its owner, and a donkey [the] manger of its master; Israel not knows, my people not considers.
pieces: An ox recognizes its owner, \q a donkey the feeding trough of its master; \q but Israel does not know, \q {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people give it no thought.

L.3: An ox knows its owner, \q and a donkey its master's manger; \q Israel does not know, \q {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people do not understand.

R.3: An ox knows who owns it. \q A donkey knows where its master feeds it. \q But the people of Israel do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q My people do not stop to think.

decisions.choice: ox and donkey: work animals that know who feeds them
decisions.reason: The ox and the donkey were the common farm animals of Israel. Even they find their way back to their owner's feeding trough; God's people do not know the one who cares for them.

decisions.choice: Israel does not know: no object is stated; the one they do not know is God, their owner
decisions.reason: "Know" has no object, which makes the charge broader: Israel does not know at all. Set beside the ox and its owner, it means Israel does not know or acknowledge the God it belongs to (Hosea 4:1, 6; Jeremiah 8:7).

decisions.choice: understand: consider, pay attention
decisions.reason: The verb means to give careful thought to something. God's people do not stop to think about who he is or what he has done.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel do not know me
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Israel" for the name Israel and supplies "me", the one Israel does not know (meaning decision m2).

records.source: ה֣וֹי׀גּ֣וֹי חֹטֵ֗א עַ֚ם כֶּ֣בֶד עָוֺ֔ן זֶ֣רַע מְרֵעִ֔ים בָּנִ֖ים מַשְׁחִיתִ֑ים עָזְב֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה נִֽאֲצ֛וּ אֶת־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נָזֹ֥רוּ אָחֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: Woe, nation sinning, people heavy of iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children acting corruptly! They have forsaken Yahweh, they have spurned [the] Holy One of Israel, they have become estranged backward.
pieces: Woe to a nation that sins, a people loaded down with guilt, \q the offspring of wrongdoers, children bent on corruption! \q They have left {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they have scorned the Holy One of Israel, they have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and gone backward.

L.4: Woe, sinning nation, people heavy with iniquity, \q offspring of evildoers, children who act corruptly! \q They have forsaken {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they have turned away backward.

R.4: How terrible it will be for this sinful nation! Their guilt is a heavy load. \q They are a family of evil people, children who do corrupt things. \q They have left {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They have treated the Holy One of Israel with scorn. They have turned their backs on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the Holy One of Israel: the God who is wholly other and pure, and who has bound himself to Israel
decisions.reason: This is Isaiah's own title for God. It appears about twenty-five times in the book, through every part of it, and only a few times elsewhere (2 Kings 19:22, which is Isaiah's word to Hezekiah; Psalms 71:22; 78:41; 89:19; Jeremiah 50:29; 51:5). "Holy" means set apart: God is unlike everything he has made and pure of every wrong, and Isaiah heard the seraphim call him "holy, holy, holy" (6:3). "Of Israel" says that this holy God has made himself Israel's own. That makes their contempt for him the more shocking here, and his promise to redeem them the more sure (41:14; 43:14).

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief over those facing judgment
decisions.reason: The word was cried out in mourning for the dead (1 Kings 13:30; Jeremiah 22:18). The prophets use it to announce disaster on those who deserve it, as if their funeral had already begun (5:8-22; Amos 5:18).

decisions.choice: estranged backward: they have turned their backs and gone away
decisions.reason: The verb means to become a stranger. With "backward" it pictures people who have turned away from God and walk off in the opposite direction (Jeremiah 7:24).

decisions.choice: turned away from him and gone backward / turned their backs on him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one they have turned from, God, which the Hebrew leaves implied.

records.source: עַ֣ל מֶ֥ה תֻכּ֛וּ ע֖וֹד תּוֹסִ֣יפוּ סָרָ֑ה כָּל־רֹ֣אשׁ לָחֳלִ֔י וְכָל־לֵבָ֖ב דַּוָּֽי׃
records.gloss: On what will you be struck again? You will add rebellion. All [the] head [is] for sickness, and all [the] heart faint.
pieces: Where else can you be struck, as you go on rebelling? \q The head is sick all over; the heart is weak through and through.

L.5: On what [part] will you be struck again, [as] you keep adding rebellion? \q The whole head [is] sick, and the whole heart faint.

R.5: Where else can you be beaten, since you keep turning against God? \q You are like a body whose head is sick all over and whose heart is weak.

decisions.choice: on what: where on the body can you still be struck
alternatives: Why will you still be struck?
decisions.reason: The two words can mean "why" or "on what". Verse 6 describes a body with no sound spot left, which favors "on what [place]": the nation has been beaten everywhere already. Read as "why", the question asks why they invite more blows by rebelling.

decisions.choice: rebellion: turning aside, revolt
decisions.reason: The noun means turning away from the right path, used of revolt against God (Deuteronomy 13:6; Jeremiah 28:16).

decisions.choice: the whole head ... the whole heart: the nation pictured as a beaten body
decisions.reason: The head and the heart stand for the whole person, from top to center. Judah is pictured as a body covered in wounds, the blows being the disasters already suffered (verse 7).

decisions.choice: turning against God ... You are like a body
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one they rebel against and explains that the head and heart are a picture of the nation.

records.source: מִכַּף־רֶ֤גֶל וְעַד־רֹאשׁ֙ אֵֽין־בּ֣וֹ מְתֹ֔ם פֶּ֥צַע וְחַבּוּרָ֖ה וּמַכָּ֣ה טְרִיָּ֑ה לֹא־זֹ֨רוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א חֻבָּ֔שׁוּ וְלֹ֥א רֻכְּכָ֖ה בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃
records.gloss: From [the] sole of [the] foot and to [the] head there is not in it soundness: bruise and welt and wound fresh; not they have been pressed out and not bound up and not softened with oil.
pieces: There is no healthy spot from the bottom of the foot up to the head: \q bruises, stripes, wounds still raw. \q No one has squeezed them clean, no one has bound them, \q no one has eased them with oil.

L.6: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it: \q bruises and welts and fresh wounds; \q they have not been pressed out, and not bound up, \q and not softened with oil.

R.6: From your feet to your head, no part of your body is healthy. \q You are covered with bruises, cuts, and fresh wounds. \q No one has cleaned them or wrapped them in bandages. \q No one has put soothing oil on them.

decisions.choice: bruise, welt, wound: the marks of a severe beating
decisions.reason: The three words describe blows: bruises, the stripes left by a lash (Proverbs 20:30), and open wounds still fresh and raw.

decisions.choice: pressed out, bound up, softened with oil: the care given to wounds
decisions.reason: A wound was cleaned by pressing out the pus, then bandaged and soothed with olive oil (Luke 10:34; Jeremiah 8:22). None of this has been done: the nation lies wounded and untended.

decisions.choice: no one has ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verbs are passive ("they have not been pressed out"). Balanced and Readable say "no one has", which keeps the sense that the wounds are left untended. Readable also says "your body" for "it".

records.source: אַרְצְכֶ֣ם שְׁמָמָ֔ה עָרֵיכֶ֖ם שְׂרֻפ֣וֹת אֵ֑שׁ אַדְמַתְכֶ֗ם לְנֶגְדְּכֶם֙ זָרִים֙ אֹכְלִ֣ים אֹתָ֔הּ וּשְׁמָמָ֖ה כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֥ת זָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: Your land [is] a desolation, your cities burned [with] fire; your ground, before you strangers [are] devouring it, and desolation like [the] overthrow of strangers.
pieces: Your country lies in ruins, \q your towns are burned down; \q foreigners eat up your fields while you watch, \q and it is ruined like a land that foreigners have torn down.

L.7: Your land [is] a desolation; \q your cities [are] burned with fire; \q your ground: before your eyes strangers are devouring it, \q and [it is] a desolation, like an overthrow by strangers.

R.7: Your country has been ruined. Your towns have been burned. \q Foreigners are taking the crops from your fields while you watch. \q Everything is destroyed, as when an enemy army tears a land apart.

decisions.choice: land desolate, cities burned: an invasion of Judah
decisions.reason: The verse describes Judah overrun by a foreign army. It fits the Assyrian invasion of 701 BC, when Sennacherib took the fortified cities of Judah (36:1) and Jerusalem alone was left standing (verse 8), though an earlier invasion is possible (2 Chronicles 28:5-18).

decisions.choice: devouring: eating up the produce
decisions.reason: The strangers "eat" the ground: they take its harvest for themselves (Deuteronomy 28:33, 51).

decisions.choice: the received text: the overthrow of strangers
decisions.reason: "Overthrow" is the word used of the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah (Deuteronomy 29:22; Amos 4:11; Isaiah 13:19), and Sodom is named in verses 9 and 10. So the text could be corrected to "like the overthrow of Sodom". But the Hebrew text has "strangers", repeating the word from earlier in the verse, and that is followed here.

decisions.choice: taking the crops ... an enemy army
decisions.reason: Readable explains "devouring" as taking the crops and "strangers" who overthrow as an enemy army.

records.source: וְנוֹתְרָ֥ה בַת־צִיּ֖וֹן כְּסֻכָּ֣ה בְכָ֑רֶם כִּמְלוּנָ֥ה בְמִקְשָׁ֖ה כְּעִ֥יר נְצוּרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And is left [the] daughter of Zion like a booth in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field, like a city besieged.
pieces: Daughter Zion is left like a shelter among the vines, \q like a hut in a cucumber patch, like a town shut in by siege.

L.8: And the daughter of Zion is left like a booth in a vineyard, \q like a hut in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.

R.8: The people of Zion are left all alone. They are like a small shelter for a watchman in a vineyard, \q or a hut in a cucumber field. They are like a city with enemies all around it.

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion: Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman
decisions.reason: Zion is the hill of Jerusalem and stands for the city. "Daughter Zion" pictures the city and its people as a young woman, loved and vulnerable (10:32; 37:22; Lamentations 2:13).

decisions.choice: a booth in a vineyard, a hut in a cucumber field: a flimsy shelter standing alone
decisions.reason: Watchmen built rough shelters of branches to guard the crops while they ripened (Job 27:18). Such a hut stood alone in the field, small and easily blown down (24:20). Jerusalem stands by itself in a ruined land.

decisions.choice: besieged: shut in by an enemy
decisions.reason: The form most likely means "besieged". It could also be read from the verb "to watch": a guarded or watched city. Either way the city is hemmed in.

decisions.choice: the people of Zion ... a small shelter for a watchman
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Zion" for "the daughter of Zion" and explains who used the shelter.

records.source: לוּלֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הוֹתִ֥יר לָ֛נוּ שָׂרִ֖יד כִּמְעָ֑ט כִּסְדֹ֣ם הָיִ֔ינוּ לַעֲמֹרָ֖ה דָּמִֽינוּ׃ס
records.gloss: If not Yahweh of hosts had left to us survivors a few, like Sodom we would have been, Gomorrah we would have resembled.
pieces: Had {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies not let a few of us survive, \q we would have shared the fate of Sodom; \q Gomorrah's end would have been ours.

L.9: If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts had not left us survivors, a few, \q we would have been like Sodom, \q we would have resembled Gomorrah.

R.9: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies let a few of us live. \q If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not, we would have been wiped out like the city of Sodom. \q We would have been destroyed like Gomorrah.

decisions.choice: Yahweh of hosts: Yahweh, commander of all the armies of heaven and earth
decisions.reason: Tseba'ot is the plural of a word for an army or a host, a great company drawn up in ranks. It is used of Israel's armies (Exodus 12:41; 1 Samuel 17:45), of the stars (Isaiah 40:26) and of the heavenly beings around God's throne (1 Kings 22:19; Psalm 103:21). Joined to God's name, it presents Yahweh as the King who commands every power in heaven and on earth: Isaiah sees him enthroned as "the King, Yahweh of hosts" (6:5). It is one of Isaiah's favorite names for God, used about sixty times in the book, and this is the first. The Septuagint of Isaiah keeps the Hebrew word, "Lord Sabaoth", and Romans 9:29 quotes this verse in that form.

decisions.choice: Sodom and Gomorrah: cities destroyed completely
decisions.reason: God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah with fire, leaving no one but Lot's family (Genesis 19:24-29). Without God's mercy Judah would have been wiped out as completely. Paul quotes the verse in Romans 9:29, where the Greek has "offspring" for "survivors".

decisions.choice: a few: going with "survivors" (a small remnant)
alternatives: we would almost have been like Sodom
decisions.reason: The word for "a little" may describe the survivors (a few of them) or go with what follows ("we would almost have been like Sodom"). The Hebrew accents join it to "survivors".

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: "Hosts" was once the ordinary word for an army, but today it most often means someone who welcomes guests, so it hides what the title says. Balanced and Readable say "Armies" here and throughout Isaiah: it states the meaning plainly and keeps the picture of a commander. "Almighty" was considered, but it turns the picture into an abstract quality. Literal keeps the traditional "the LORD of hosts".

decisions.choice: wiped out ... destroyed
decisions.reason: Readable says what it meant to be like Sodom and Gomorrah: to be destroyed.

records.source: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם הַאֲזִ֛ינוּ תּוֹרַ֥ת אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ עַ֥ם עֲמֹרָֽה׃
records.gloss: Hear [the] word of Yahweh, rulers of Sodom; give ear [to the] instruction of our God, people of Gomorrah.
pieces: Rulers of Sodom, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q People of Gomorrah, open your ears to the instruction of our God!

L.10: Hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you rulers of Sodom; \q give ear to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!

R.10: You leaders are like the rulers of Sodom. Listen to the message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q You people are like the people of Gomorrah. Listen to what our God is teaching you!

decisions.choice: rulers of Sodom, people of Gomorrah: Jerusalem's leaders and people, as wicked as those cities
decisions.reason: Verse 9 said Judah escaped Sodom's fate. Now its rulers and people are called by those names, because their deeds are like Sodom's (3:9; Ezekiel 16:46-50).

decisions.choice: instruction: teaching from God
decisions.reason: The word torah means instruction or teaching. Here it is the teaching God gives through the prophet in the verses that follow (compare 2:3; 8:16, 20).

decisions.choice: You leaders are like ... You people are like
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the names are a comparison: Jerusalem's leaders and people are not literally in Sodom and Gomorrah.

records.heading: Sacrifices that give no pleasure

records.source: לָמָּה־לִּ֤י רֹב־זִבְחֵיכֶם֙ יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׂבַ֛עְתִּי עֹל֥וֹת אֵילִ֖ים וְחֵ֣לֶב מְרִיאִ֑ים וְדַ֨ם פָּרִ֧ים וּכְבָשִׂ֛ים וְעַתּוּדִ֖ים לֹ֥א חָפָֽצְתִּי׃
records.gloss: Why to me [the] multitude of your sacrifices? says Yahweh. I am sated [with] burnt offerings of rams and [the] fat of fatlings; and [the] blood of bulls and lambs and goats not I delight in.
pieces: What use to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} are all your sacrifices? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I have had all I want of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened beasts; \q the blood of bulls and lambs and goats gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no pleasure.

L.11: What [is] the multitude of your sacrifices to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened animals, \q and in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats I take no delight.

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says: Why do you bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} so many sacrifices? \q I have had all I want of the rams you burn on the altar and the fat of your fattened animals. \q I do not enjoy the blood of your bulls, lambs, and goats.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings, fat, blood: the parts of a sacrifice given to God
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was burned whole on the altar (Leviticus 1). In other sacrifices the fat was burned for God and the blood poured out at the altar, since both belonged to him (Leviticus 3:16-17).

decisions.choice: I take no delight: God rejects worship offered by people who do injustice
decisions.reason: God had commanded these sacrifices. What he rejects is worship from hands full of blood (verse 15), offered by people who neglect justice (verses 16-17). Other prophets say the same (1 Samuel 15:22; Hosea 6:6; Amos 5:21-24; Micah 6:6-8).

decisions.choice: The LORD says ... the rams you burn on the altar
decisions.reason: Readable puts "the LORD says" first and explains what a burnt offering was.

records.source: כִּ֣י תָבֹ֔אוּ לֵרָא֖וֹת פָּנָ֑י מִי־בִקֵּ֥שׁ זֹ֛את מִיֶּדְכֶ֖ם רְמֹ֥ס חֲצֵרָֽי׃
records.gloss: When you come to appear [before] my face, who has required this from your hand, to trample my courts?
pieces: You come to stand in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence; \q but who told you to do this, to tread down {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} courtyards?

L.12: When you come to appear before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q who has required this from your hand, to trample {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} courts?

R.12: You come to the temple to stand before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q But I never asked you to bring all this and trample through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} courtyards.

decisions.choice: to appear before me: to come to the temple to worship
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of coming to the sanctuary at the feasts (Exodus 23:15, 17; Deuteronomy 16:16). The consonants could also be read "to see my face", and the verb may first have been read that way (Psalm 42:3).

decisions.choice: my courts: the open courtyards of the temple
decisions.reason: Worshipers stood in the temple courtyards with their offerings (Psalm 84:3, 11; 100:4). Without justice their coming is only the trampling of feet, like animals tramping through the courts.

decisions.choice: I never asked you
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question "who has required this?" into the statement it implies, and names the temple.

records.source: לֹ֣א תוֹסִ֗יפוּ הָבִיא֙ מִנְחַת־שָׁ֔וְא קְטֹ֧רֶת תּוֹעֵבָ֛ה הִ֖יא לִ֑י חֹ֤דֶשׁ וְשַׁבָּת֙ קְרֹ֣א מִקְרָ֔א לֹא־אוּכַ֥ל אָ֖וֶן וַעֲצָרָֽה׃
records.gloss: Not you must again bring an offering of emptiness; incense, an abomination it [is] to me. New moon and sabbath, [the] calling of assembly: not I can [bear] iniquity and solemn assembly.
pieces: Bring no more empty gifts; \q to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the smoke of incense is loathsome. \q New moon, Sabbath, the call to assemble: \q wrongdoing and holy gatherings together are more than I can bear.

L.13: Do not again bring an offering of emptiness; \q incense is an abomination to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q New moon and Sabbath, the calling of an assembly: \q I cannot bear wickedness and a solemn assembly.

R.13: Stop bringing {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} offerings that mean nothing. \q I hate the smell of your incense. \q You keep the new moon festivals and the Sabbath days. You call people together to worship. \q But you also do evil things, and I cannot stand worship mixed with evil.

decisions.choice: an offering of emptiness: a gift that means nothing
decisions.reason: The offering is the gift brought to God, often of grain (Leviticus 2). "Emptiness" means what is worthless or false: the gift has no value because the giver's life denies it.

decisions.choice: new moon and Sabbath: the monthly and weekly holy days
decisions.reason: The first day of each month and the seventh day of each week were kept with offerings and rest (Numbers 28:9-15; Amos 8:5).

decisions.choice: wickedness and solemn assembly: worship and evil side by side
decisions.reason: The two nouns are joined: God cannot bear sacred gatherings kept by people who do wrong. The Septuagint has "fasting and idleness" here, reading a different word for the first one.

decisions.choice: you also do evil things ... worship mixed with evil
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the joining of wickedness and worship in short sentences.

records.source: חָדְשֵׁיכֶ֤ם וּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם֙ שָׂנְאָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֔י הָי֥וּ עָלַ֖י לָטֹ֑רַח נִלְאֵ֖יתִי נְשֹֽׂא׃
records.gloss: Your new moons and your appointed feasts hates my soul; they have become on me a burden; I am weary of bearing [them].
pieces: Your new moons and your fixed feasts are hateful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, to the depths of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul; \q they lie on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like a heavy load, \q and I am tired of carrying it.

L.14: Your new moons and your appointed feasts {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul hates; \q they have become a burden upon {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q I am weary of carrying [them].

R.14: I truly hate your new moon festivals and your other holy days. \q They have become a heavy load for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I am tired of carrying it.

decisions.choice: my soul hates: I hate with my whole self
decisions.reason: The "soul" is the self, the whole living person. "My soul hates" is stronger than "I hate" (compare Leviticus 26:11, 30; Psalm 11:5).

decisions.choice: your new moons and your feasts: no longer God's feasts but theirs
decisions.reason: In the Law these are "my appointed feasts", the feasts of Yahweh (Leviticus 23:2). Kept without justice, they have become the people's own and no longer honor God (compare Amos 5:21).

decisions.choice: truly hate
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of "my soul hates" without the word "soul".

records.source: וּבְפָרִשְׂכֶ֣ם כַּפֵּיכֶ֗ם אַעְלִ֤ים עֵינַי֙ מִכֶּ֔ם גַּ֛ם כִּֽי־תַרְבּ֥וּ תְפִלָּ֖ה אֵינֶ֣נִּי שֹׁמֵ֑עַ יְדֵיכֶ֖ם דָּמִ֥ים מָלֵֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: And when you spread out your palms, I will hide my eyes from you; even though you multiply prayer, not I [am] listening; your hands [with] blood are full.
pieces: Spread out your palms, and I will hide {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes from you; \q pile up prayer upon prayer, and I will not be listening. \q Blood fills your hands.

L.15: And when you spread out your palms, I will hide {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes from you; \q even when you multiply prayer, I am not listening. \q Your hands are full of blood.

R.15: When you raise your hands to pray, I will look away. \q You may pray many prayers, but I will not listen. \q Your hands are covered with blood from the violence you do.

decisions.choice: spread out your palms: the posture of prayer
decisions.reason: People prayed standing with open hands lifted toward heaven (Exodus 9:29; 1 Kings 8:22, 38).

decisions.choice: blood: bloodshed, violence against people
decisions.reason: The plural form of "blood" means blood shed by violence and the guilt of it (Exodus 22:1; Isaiah 59:3). Verses 17, 21 and 23 show who has been harmed: the orphan, the widow, the victims of murderers. It also stands against the blood of the sacrifices in verse 11.

decisions.choice: I am not listening: God goes on refusing to hear
decisions.reason: The participle describes a settled state: while they keep praying, God keeps not listening (compare 59:2).

decisions.choice: blood from the violence you do
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the blood is from violence against people, not from the sacrifices (meaning decision m2).

records.source: רַחֲצוּ֙ הִזַּכּ֔וּ הָסִ֛ירוּ רֹ֥עַ מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם מִנֶּ֣גֶד עֵינָ֑י חִדְל֖וּ הָרֵֽעַ׃
records.gloss: Wash, make yourselves clean; remove [the] evil of your deeds from before my eyes; cease to do evil.
pieces: Wash, and be clean again! \q Clear your wicked deeds away from before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes. \q Put an end to evil.

L.16: Wash, make yourselves clean; \q remove the evil of your deeds from before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes; \q cease to do evil.

R.16: Wash yourselves and become clean! \q Get rid of the evil things you do. I do not want to see them anymore. \q Stop doing evil.

decisions.choice: wash, make yourselves clean: turn from your sins
decisions.reason: Washing was part of becoming ritually clean (Leviticus 14:8-9). Here it pictures a moral cleansing: hands full of blood (verse 15) are to be washed by turning from evil (Psalm 51:4, 9; Jeremiah 4:14).

decisions.choice: a series of commands running into verse 17
decisions.reason: Nine commands follow one another without a break, from "wash" to "plead for the widow". The first four say turn from evil; the last five say do good.

records.source: לִמְד֥וּ הֵיטֵ֛ב דִּרְשׁ֥וּ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט אַשְּׁר֣וּ חָמ֑וֹץ שִׁפְט֣וּ יָת֔וֹם רִ֖יבוּ אַלְמָנָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Learn to do good; seek justice; set right [the] oppressor; judge [the] fatherless; plead [for the] widow.
pieces: Learn to do good. Go after justice. Set the oppressor straight. \q Give the fatherless child a fair hearing; stand up for the widow in court.

L.17: Learn to do good; seek justice; set right the oppressor; \q defend the fatherless; plead the widow's case.

R.17: Learn to do what is good. Work hard to make things fair. Stop people who mistreat others. \q Defend the rights of children whose fathers have died. Speak up for widows when they are treated unfairly.

decisions.choice: set right the oppressor: correct the one who crushes others
decisions.reason: The verb means to make go straight. The noun is read as "the oppressor", one who crushes others. With a small change in the vowels it would be "the oppressed", and the command would be to set the oppressed right, that is, to help them; the Septuagint reads it that way ("rescue the one wronged").

decisions.choice: the fatherless and the widow: those with no man to defend them in court
decisions.reason: In Israel a woman or child without a husband or father had no one to speak for them in court and could easily be cheated. God commands that they be protected and calls himself their defender (Exodus 22:21-23; Deuteronomy 10:18; 24:17).

decisions.choice: judge, plead: take up their legal case
decisions.reason: "Judge" here means to give someone their rights in court; "plead" means to take up their case as their advocate.

decisions.choice: fatherless child ... in court / children whose fathers have died
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly who the fatherless are and that these are legal cases.

records.source: לְכוּ־נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אִם־יִֽהְי֨וּ חֲטָאֵיכֶ֤ם כַּשָּׁנִים֙ כַּשֶּׁ֣לֶג יַלְבִּ֔ינוּ אִם־יַאְדִּ֥ימוּ כַתּוֹלָ֖ע כַּצֶּ֥מֶר יִהְיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: Come please, and let us argue together, says Yahweh: if they are your sins like scarlet, like snow they will be white; if they are red like crimson, like wool they will be.
pieces: Come, let us take this matter to court together, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Your sins may be scarlet, yet they will turn white as snow; \q though they are as red as crimson dye, they will be like undyed wool.

L.18: Come now, and let us argue [it] out together, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Though your sins are like scarlet, like snow they will be white; \q though they are red like crimson, like wool they will become.

R.18: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says: Come, let us settle this matter between us. \q Your sins are like cloth dyed bright red. But they will become white like snow. \q They are dark red, but they will become white like wool.

decisions.choice: let us argue it out: settle the case at law
decisions.reason: The verb belongs to the law court: to present a case and reach a verdict (Micah 6:2; Job 23:7). It continues the lawsuit that began in verse 2. God summons Judah to settle the case with him.

decisions.choice: though ... they will be white: an offer of cleansing
alternatives: If your sins are like scarlet, can they be white as snow?
decisions.reason: Read with verses 19-20, the clauses are an offer: though their sins are deep red, God will make them white, if they are willing and obey. The words can also be read as a pointed question ("If your sins are like scarlet, can they become white as snow?"), meaning they cannot be cleansed while Judah goes on as it is.

decisions.choice: scarlet, crimson: deep red dyes
decisions.reason: Scarlet and crimson dye came from an insect and gave cloth a bright red that did not wash out. The contrast is with the white of snow and of wool before it is dyed (Psalm 51:9). Red may also recall the blood on their hands (verse 15).

decisions.choice: crimson dye ... undyed wool / cloth dyed bright red
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the colors are dyes in cloth, which is what makes the picture work.

records.source: אִם־תֹּאב֖וּ וּשְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם ט֥וּב הָאָ֖רֶץ תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: If you are willing and you listen, [the] good of the land you will eat.
pieces: If you consent and listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q you will eat the rich produce of the land.

L.19: If you are willing and you listen, \q the good [things] of the land you will eat.

R.19: If you choose to obey {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q you will have plenty of good food from your land.

decisions.choice: listen: obey
decisions.reason: To "listen" to God means to do what he says (Exodus 19:5; Deuteronomy 11:13).

decisions.choice: eat the good of the land: the blessing promised for obedience
decisions.reason: The Law promised the produce of the land to an obedient people and the sword to a rebellious one (Leviticus 26:3-8, 25; Deuteronomy 28:1-14). Verse 20 makes a play on "eat": eat the land's good, or be eaten by the sword.

decisions.choice: listen to me / obey me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "me", God, who is speaking.

records.source: וְאִם־תְּמָאֲנ֖וּ וּמְרִיתֶ֑ם חֶ֣רֶב תְּאֻכְּל֔וּ כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ס
records.gloss: And if you refuse and you rebel, [by the] sword you will be eaten; for [the] mouth of Yahweh has spoken.
pieces: But if you say no and rebel, \q the sword will eat you up; \q for the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.

L.20: But if you refuse and rebel, \q [by the] sword you will be eaten, \q for the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.

R.20: But if you refuse and turn against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q enemies will kill you in war. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} has said this.

decisions.choice: eaten by the sword: killed in war
decisions.reason: The sword is said to "eat" those it kills (Deuteronomy 32:42; 2 Samuel 2:26). It answers verse 19: if they obey they will eat; if they rebel they will be eaten.

decisions.choice: the mouth of Yahweh has spoken: the word is certain
decisions.reason: The phrase closes a word of God and seals it as sure to happen (40:5; 58:14; Micah 4:4).

decisions.choice: turn against me ... enemies will kill you in war
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one they rebel against and explains the sword as enemies in war.

records.source: אֵיכָה֙ הָיְתָ֣ה לְזוֹנָ֔ה קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה מְלֵאֲתִ֣י מִשְׁפָּ֗ט צֶ֛דֶק יָלִ֥ין בָּ֖הּ וְעַתָּ֥ה מְרַצְּחִֽים׃
records.gloss: How she has become a prostitute, [the] town faithful, full of justice! Righteousness lodged in her, and now murderers.
pieces: How the faithful town has turned prostitute! \q Justice filled her once; righteousness made its home in her. Now it is murderers.

L.21: How she has become a prostitute, the faithful town, \q [she who was] full of justice! Righteousness lodged in her, but now murderers.

R.21: How sad! Jerusalem used to be faithful to God, but now it is like a prostitute. \q It was full of justice, and righteousness lived there. But now murderers live there.

decisions.choice: how: a cry of lament
decisions.reason: The word opens a funeral song over something lost (Lamentations 1:1; 2:1; 2 Samuel 1:19). Verses 21-26 mourn the city before announcing its restoration.

decisions.choice: the faithful town has become a prostitute: Jerusalem unfaithful to God
decisions.reason: The prophets picture God's people as a wife and their unfaithfulness as prostitution (Hosea 2:4-7; Jeremiah 3:1-3; Ezekiel 16). Here the unfaithfulness is shown in injustice and murder rather than in worship of other gods.

decisions.choice: lodged: lived, made its home
decisions.reason: The verb means to spend the night or to stay. Righteousness once lived in the city; now murderers do.

decisions.choice: How sad! Jerusalem ... faithful to God ... like a prostitute
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the lament cry, names the city, says to whom it was faithful, and makes the picture a comparison.

records.heading: The faithful town gone astray

records.source: כַּסְפֵּ֖ךְ הָיָ֣ה לְסִיגִ֑ים סָבְאֵ֖ךְ מָה֥וּל בַּמָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Your silver has become dross; your drink mixed with water.
pieces: Your silver has turned to slag; \q your wine is cut with water.

L.22: Your silver has become dross; \q your drink [is] mixed with water.

R.22: Jerusalem, you were like pure silver, but now you are like the waste left over when silver is melted. \q You were like good wine, but now you are like wine mixed with water.

decisions.choice: dross: the waste skimmed off when silver is refined
decisions.reason: When silver ore is melted, the impurities rise and are taken off as worthless dross (Proverbs 25:4; Ezekiel 22:18-22). Verse 25 returns to the picture.

decisions.choice: drink: wine or beer
decisions.reason: The word means a strong drink, such as wine or beer (Hosea 4:18; Nahum 1:10). Wine thinned with water has lost its strength and value.

decisions.choice: silver and wine: the city itself, which has lost its worth
decisions.reason: The two pictures describe what Jerusalem has become, as verse 23 explains: what was valuable has become cheap. They may also hint at merchants who cheated with poor silver and watered wine.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem, you were like pure silver ... You were like good wine
decisions.reason: Readable names the city and makes both pictures comparisons. Balanced says "slag" and "wine"; Literal keeps "dross" and "drink".

records.source: שָׂרַ֣יִךְ סוֹרְרִ֗ים וְחַבְרֵי֙ גַּנָּבִ֔ים כֻּלּוֹ֙ אֹהֵ֣ב שֹׁ֔חַד וְרֹדֵ֖ף שַׁלְמֹנִ֑ים יָתוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁפֹּ֔טוּ וְרִ֥יב אַלְמָנָ֖ה לֹֽא־יָב֥וֹא אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: Your princes [are] rebels and companions of thieves; all of it loves a bribe and pursues rewards; [the] fatherless not they judge, and [the] case of [the] widow not comes to them.
pieces: Your leaders are in revolt and keep company with thieves. \q All of them love a bribe and go hunting for payoffs. \q The fatherless get no justice from them; \q the widow's lawsuit is never heard in their court.

L.23: Your princes [are] rebels and companions of thieves; \q every one of them loves a bribe and chases after payoffs. \q The fatherless they do not defend, \q and the widow's case does not come before them.

R.23: Your leaders refuse to obey God. They are friends with thieves. \q They all love it when people pay them money to do wrong. They are always looking for gifts. \q They do not protect children who have no father. \q They will not even listen when a widow brings them her problem.

decisions.choice: your princes are rebels: a play on sound
decisions.reason: The words for "princes" and "rebels" sound alike (sarayikh sorerim), as in Hosea 9:15. The leaders who should keep order are themselves stubborn rebels against God.

decisions.choice: bribe, rewards: payments to judges for a favorable verdict
decisions.reason: The Law forbade judges to take a bribe, because it blinds the eyes of the wise (Exodus 23:8; Deuteronomy 16:19). The word for "rewards" is found only here; it means payments or gifts.

decisions.choice: the widow's case does not come to them: they will not hear it
decisions.reason: The widow's lawsuit never reaches the judges, either because they refuse to hear it or because she has nothing to pay them. Compare verse 17, where these are the very cases they are to take up.

decisions.choice: refuse to obey God ... pay them money to do wrong
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one they rebel against and explains what a bribe is.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲבִ֖יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ה֚וֹי אֶנָּחֵ֣ם מִצָּרַ֔י וְאִנָּקְמָ֖ה מֵאוֹיְבָֽי׃
records.gloss: Therefore, [the] declaration of the Lord GOD of hosts, [the] Mighty One of Israel: Woe! I will relieve myself of my foes, and I will avenge myself on my enemies.
pieces: So the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: \q Woe to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} foes! I will be rid of them at last; \q I will pay back {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} enemies.

L.24: Therefore, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: \q Woe! I will get relief from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} adversaries, \q and I will avenge {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} enemies.

R.24: So the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says: \q How terrible it will be for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} enemies! I will be rid of them. \q I will punish those who are against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: my foes, my enemies: the wicked within Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The enemies God will deal with are not a foreign army but the corrupt leaders and murderers of Jerusalem (verses 21-23). By their injustice God's own people have made themselves his enemies. The judgment that follows is a refining (verses 25-26).

decisions.choice: the Mighty One of Israel: the God who is Israel's strength
decisions.reason: The title echoes "the Mighty One of Jacob" (Genesis 49:24; Psalm 132:2, 5; Isaiah 49:26; 60:16). Only here is it "of Israel". It stands beside "Yahweh of hosts" to stress God's power.

decisions.choice: woe ... I will relieve myself: God's patience with evil comes to an end
decisions.reason: The same cry as in verse 4. The verb means to be comforted or eased: God will find relief from the wrong that has burdened him (verse 14).

decisions.choice: the Lord GOD of hosts / of Armies
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "the Lord" followed by God's name. Where the name follows "Lord" it is printed "GOD", as elsewhere, to avoid "the Lord LORD". Balanced and Readable say "Armies" (see 1:9).

decisions.choice: Woe to my foes / How terrible it will be for my enemies
decisions.reason: The cry "woe" stands alone in the Hebrew. Balanced and Readable join it to the enemies it is aimed at.

records.source: וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה יָדִי֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ וְאֶצְרֹ֥ף כַּבֹּ֖ר סִיגָ֑יִךְ וְאָסִ֖ירָה כָּל־בְּדִילָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: And I will turn my hand against you, and I will smelt like lye your dross, and I will remove all your alloy.
pieces: I will turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against you; \q I will melt away your slag as with lye and clear out all your impure metal.

L.25: And I will turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against you, \q and I will smelt away your dross as with lye, \q and I will remove all your alloy.

R.25: I will use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power against you. \q I will purify you, the way silver is melted down and cleaned. \q I will take away everything worthless in you.

decisions.choice: turn my hand against you: act against you
decisions.reason: To turn the hand against someone is to strike them (Amos 1:8; Psalm 81:15). Here the blow is meant to purify, not to destroy.

decisions.choice: smelt as with lye: refine silver with a flux
alternatives: I will smelt your dross in the furnace
decisions.reason: Lye or potash was added to molten metal as a flux, to draw out the impurities. With a small change the word would read "in the furnace". Either way the picture is of silver being refined (48:10; Malachi 3:2-3).

decisions.choice: alloy: base metal mixed with the silver
decisions.reason: The word is used of tin or lead, cheaper metals mixed into the silver that must be removed (Ezekiel 22:18, 20). It answers verse 22: "your silver has become dross".

decisions.choice: use my power ... the way silver is melted down and cleaned
decisions.reason: Readable explains the hand as power and turns the refining into a comparison.

records.source: וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה שֹׁפְטַ֨יִךְ֙ כְּבָרִ֣אשֹׁנָ֔ה וְיֹעֲצַ֖יִךְ כְּבַתְּחִלָּ֑ה אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן יִקָּ֤רֵא לָךְ֙ עִ֣יר הַצֶּ֔דֶק קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning; after thus you will be called City of Righteousness, Town Faithful.
pieces: I will give you back judges like those you had at first, \q and counselors like those at the start. \q Then you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful Town.

L.26: And I will restore your judges as at the first, \q and your counselors as at the beginning. \q After this you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful Town.

R.26: I will give you good judges and wise advisers again, like the ones you had long ago. \q Then you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful Town.

decisions.choice: the Faithful Town: verse 21 reversed
decisions.reason: "Faithful town" is the phrase of verse 21, where the city had become a prostitute. The passage ends where it began, with the city faithful again.

decisions.choice: judges and counselors: the city's leaders
decisions.reason: Judges decided cases; counselors advised the king. "As at the first" looks back to the city's early days, when justice was done, perhaps the reign of David (2 Samuel 8:15).

decisions.choice: you will be called: you will truly be
decisions.reason: A new name declares what the city will be (compare 60:14; 62:4, 12).

records.source: צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה וְשָׁבֶ֖יהָ בִּצְדָקָֽה׃
records.gloss: Zion with justice will be redeemed, and her returning ones with righteousness.
pieces: Justice will set Zion free, \q and righteousness will free those of her people who turn back.

L.27: Zion will be redeemed with justice, \q and her returning ones with righteousness.

R.27: Justice will rescue Zion. \q Righteousness will rescue the people there who turn back to God.

decisions.choice: redeemed: set free, ransomed
decisions.reason: The verb means to set free by paying a price, as a firstborn or a slave was ransomed (Exodus 13:13; Deuteronomy 7:8).

decisions.choice: with justice ... with righteousness: by the justice done in judgment and restored in the city
decisions.reason: Zion is freed by justice: God's judgment that removes the wicked (verses 24-25, 28) and the right judges he restores (verse 26). It is not said whose justice it is, and both may be meant.

decisions.choice: her returning ones: those who turn back to God
decisions.reason: The word means those who turn or return. In this passage it most likely means those who repent, set against those who forsake Yahweh (verse 28). It can also mean those who come back from exile.

decisions.choice: turn back to God
decisions.reason: Readable names the one they turn back to (meaning decision m3).

records.source: וְשֶׁ֧בֶר פֹּשְׁעִ֛ים וְחַטָּאִ֖ים יַחְדָּ֑ו וְעֹזְבֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יִכְלֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And [a] breaking of rebels and sinners together, and those forsaking Yahweh will come to an end.
pieces: Rebels and sinners alike will be crushed, \q and all who walk away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be finished.

L.28: But [there will be] a breaking of rebels and sinners together, \q and those who forsake {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will come to an end.

R.28: But all who rebel and sin will be destroyed. \q People who turn away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be gone.

decisions.choice: a breaking: the verse begins with a noun
decisions.reason: The verse has no verb in its first half: "a breaking of rebels and sinners". It is a short, sharp announcement of their end.

decisions.choice: rebels ... those who forsake Yahweh: the people of verses 2 and 4
decisions.reason: The words echo the charge at the start of the chapter: "they have rebelled against me" (verse 2), "they have forsaken Yahweh" (verse 4). Zion will be redeemed (verse 27), but not those who will not turn.

records.source: כִּ֣י יֵבֹ֔שׁוּ מֵאֵילִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֲמַדְתֶּ֑ם וְתַ֨חְפְּר֔וּ מֵהַגַּנּ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּחַרְתֶּֽם׃
records.gloss: For they will be ashamed of [the] oaks which you desired, and you will blush for the gardens which you chose.
pieces: Yes, the oaks you set your heart on will bring you shame; \q the gardens you chose will make you blush.

L.29: For they will be ashamed of the oaks which you desired, \q and you will be abashed for the gardens which you chose.

R.29: You loved to worship false gods under big trees and in special gardens. \q But you will be ashamed of those trees and gardens.

decisions.choice: oaks and gardens: places where other gods were worshiped
decisions.reason: Great trees and planted groves were favorite places for the worship of other gods (Deuteronomy 12:2; Hosea 4:13; Isaiah 57:5; 65:3; 66:17). The people chose and loved them; they will be ashamed of them.

decisions.choice: they ... you: a change of person
alternatives: they will be ashamed ... you desired (different groups)
decisions.reason: The verse begins with "they" and goes on with "you", a change common in the prophets' poetry. Both refer to the same people.

decisions.choice: you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "you" throughout, as the verse goes on, since both refer to the same people (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps "they".

decisions.choice: worship false gods under big trees
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the oaks and gardens were for (meaning decision m1).

records.source: כִּ֣י תִֽהְי֔וּ כְּאֵלָ֖ה נֹבֶ֣לֶת עָלֶ֑הָ וּֽכְגַנָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־מַ֖יִם אֵ֥ין לָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: For you will be like an oak withering its leaf, and like a garden which water there is not for it.
pieces: You yourselves will be like an oak whose leaves are drying up, \q like a garden left without water.

L.30: For you will be like an oak whose leaf is withering, \q and like a garden that has no water.

R.30: You will become like a tree whose leaves dry up, \q or like a garden that gets no water.

decisions.choice: like an oak, like a garden: they become like what they worshiped
decisions.reason: The oaks and gardens of verse 29 now picture the worshipers themselves, dry and dying. Those who trust Yahweh are instead like a well-watered tree or garden (Psalm 1:3; Jeremiah 17:8; Isaiah 58:11).

records.source: וְהָיָ֤ה הֶחָסֹן֙ לִנְעֹ֔רֶת וּפֹעֲל֖וֹ לְנִיצ֑וֹץ וּבָעֲר֧וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם יַחְדָּ֖ו וְאֵ֥ין מְכַבֶּֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And will become the strong [one] tinder, and his work a spark, and they will burn the two of them together, and there is not [one who] quenches.
pieces: Whoever is strong will become tinder, and what he has made will be the spark; \q the two will burn together, and there will be no one to put out the flames.

L.31: And the strong will become tinder, and his work a spark, \q and the two of them will burn together, with no one to quench [them].

R.31: Powerful people will burn like dry straw. The things they have made will be the spark that starts the fire. \q Both will burn together, and no one will put out the fire.

decisions.choice: the strong: the powerful man
decisions.reason: The word means strong or mighty. It is used of oaks in Amos 2:9, so it may continue the picture of the great tree (verse 30), here standing for the powerful people of Judah.

decisions.choice: his work: what he has made, perhaps his idols
decisions.reason: The noun means work or deed. After verse 29 it may mean the idols and holy places the powerful have made; it may mean all their deeds. The man and his work become fuel and fire for each other.

decisions.choice: tinder: the fibers of flax, which catch fire at once
decisions.reason: The word means the loose fibers shaken from flax (Judges 16:9). They burn up in an instant.

decisions.choice: dry straw
decisions.reason: Readable compares the tinder to dry straw, something every reader knows burns quickly.
